title: Relative uses ChatGPT to navigate literature during FOLFIRINOX; pancreatic liver metastases regress, contribution undetermined
summary: A dentist nephew in Baku used ChatGPT, later GPT-5, to summarize literature and weigh off-label add-ons for a 65-year-old on FOLFIRINOX; 11 liver metastases regressed; the author cannot attribute it.
account: Khalil (International Medical Case Reports Journal, 2026) is a dentist and the patient's nephew writing as sole author. He reports a 65-year-old with metastatic pancreatic adenosquamous carcinoma and 11 hepatic metastases treated with FOLFIRINOX. The patient and author added high-dose intravenous vitamin C, doxycycline and later azithromycin as off-label home measures. After three cycles magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed complete radiological regression of the hepatic lesions, confirmed around the sixth cycle. Chemotherapy stopped after six cycles. Cholestasis and a rise in CA 19-9 in late September 2025 initially suggested recurrence. After ursodeoxycholic acid, CA 19-9 normalized by 10 January 2026. The author and patient used ChatGPT, initially an earlier model and later GPT-5. They used it to search and summarize literature, interpret CA 19–9 during cholestasis and appraise data on adjunctive interventions. The author writes that GPT “materially influenced how we navigated information”. He also states that the single case cannot determine the contribution of those interventions to the response. No attributable change in diagnosis or treatment can be established from the sources on record. Follow-up MRI on 20 February 2026 showed no visible hepatic lesions.

fields.account: Khalil (International Medical Case Reports Journal, 2026) is a dentist and the patient's nephew writing as sole author. He reports a 65-year-old with metastatic pancreatic adenosquamous carcinoma and 11 hepatic metastases treated with FOLFIRINOX. The patient and author added high-dose intravenous vitamin C, doxycycline and later azithromycin as off-label home measures. After three cycles magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed complete radiological regression of the hepatic lesions, confirmed around the sixth cycle. Chemotherapy stopped after six cycles. Cholestasis and a rise in CA 19-9 in late September 2025 initially suggested recurrence. After ursodeoxycholic acid, CA 19-9 normalized by 10 January 2026. The author and patient used ChatGPT, initially an earlier model and later GPT-5. They used it to search and summarize literature, interpret CA 19–9 during cholestasis and appraise data on adjunctive interventions. The author writes that GPT “materially influenced how we navigated information”. He also states that the single case cannot determine the contribution of those interventions to the response. No attributable change in diagnosis or treatment can be established from the sources on record. Follow-up MRI on 20 February 2026 showed no visible hepatic lesions.
